answer:
On MinGW/Windows, the runtime does not define `LC_MESSAGES`. GNU gettext therefore defines it to the arbitrary value `1729`:

```c
#define LC_MESSAGES 1729
```

This value is only an identifier for the message-locale category; it is not a Windows locale value. For `gettext` and `dgettext`, the category is `LC_MESSAGES`, and the locale name is obtained through:

```c
setlocale(LC_MESSAGES, NULL)
```

Catalogs are located using paths of the form:

```text
dir_name/locale/LC_MESSAGES/domain_name.mo
```

On Windows, gettext may determine the default locale from the thread locale when no environment variables or `setlocale()` calls are used.
